title: Optometry - Discharge - Helen Morris
writingTask: Using the information in the case notes, write a discharge letter to Mr Daniel Price, Community Optometrist, York Vision Practice, 17 Stonegate, York, summarising Mrs Morris's post-operative optometric care, current visual status and follow-up recommendations.
caseNotes: Read the case notes below and complete the writing task which follows.
You are an optometrist working in a hospital low-vision and refraction clinic. Mrs Helen Morris has completed a
short episode of care following bilateral cataract surgery.
Independent with activities of daily living
OCULAR HISTORY: Bilateral age-related cataracts diagnosed 2025
Right phacoemulsification with intraocular lens - 4 May 2026
Left phacoemulsification with intraocular lens - 8 June 2026
Anterior chambers quiet; intraocular lenses centred
Difficulty reading small print for long periods
No photopsia, floaters, pain or redness
Advised preservative-free lubricants up to four times daily as required
Discussed good lighting and regular breaks for prolonged reading
Reading and computer use back to usual level
Ocular health stable; no further hospital optometry input required
Discharged to routine community optometric care
Recommend eye examination every 2 years, or earlier if symptomatic
Seek urgent review for sudden vision loss, flashes, floaters, pain or persistent

candidateLetter:
Mr Daniel Price
York Vision Practice
York

Re: Discharge

Dear Daniel,

I am writing about Mrs Helen Morris (DOB 27/04/1956). She is married and she is a retired primary school teacher. She has high cholesterol and mild arthritis in her hands but she is independant with daily living.

At the last visit on 28/07/26 she was comfortable with her new glasses and her reading and computer use were back to normal. VA 6/6 both eyes, eyes stable. Dry eye only sometimes now.

Her cataracts was diagnosed in 2025. The left eye was operated on 4 May 2026 and the right eye on 8 June 2026. Both eyes had phacoemulsification with an intraocular lens. After the surgery she had mild dry eye symptoms.

22/06/26 review - unaided R 6/9 L 6/9, best corrected 6/6 each eye. Her near vision was N5 with a +3.00 add. The anterior chambers were quiet, the IOLs were centred and there was no retinal or macular abnormality. She was super happy with her distance vision but the poor lady was struggling to read small print for long periods. Also she have some grittiness in the evenings and she still gets floaters sometimes.

On 30/06/26 we done the final refraction and she recieved a new progressive prescription. We advised her about good lighting and taking regular breaks when reading for a long time. We also talked about her dry eye.

She is now discharged from our clinic to community care. You can see her whenever you think it is needed.

Thank you so much for your help and have a lovely day!!

Yours faithfully,

Optometrist
